messages:
Ada: Heads-up — CI perf alert on PR-9501 microbench run (kv_batcher_wait_time_p95). Threshold diff +28% on the PR run vs baseline. See artifact ci.perf/9501.
perf-bot: [automated] perf-regression: kv_batcher_wait_time_p95 exceeded threshold (baseline 3.4ms -> 4.4ms). Build: ci.perf/9501, job: microperf/kv-batcher
Frank: taking a look. Was this a merge with recent batching/kernel changes? pinging @Sasha @Devon
Sasha: quick glance: PR-9499 (kernel-affinity heuristics) and PR-9478 (batching sampler tweak) merged in last deploy window. Might be interaction.
Devon: I repro'd locally on my perf bench. Baseline (main at commit abc123): p95 ~3.3ms. With PR-9501 merge onto main I get p95 ~4.2ms. CPU/GPU utilization looks unchanged.
Ada: Can you paste the microbench output snippet?
Devon: log:
```
kv_batcher: n=100k
baseline: p50=1.2ms p95=3.3ms p99=6.8ms
pr-9501:  p50=1.3ms p95=4.2ms p99=8.9ms
kv_cache_hit_rate: baseline=82.1% pr=57.8%
batcher_wait_time_avg: baseline=0.8ms pr=1.6ms
```
Frank: whoa — KV hit rate drop looks huge. Could be eviction/affinity change leading to different key partitioning.
Sasha: I instrumented the kernel selector. For short sequences (<64 tokens) PR-9499 prefers kernel_B instead of kernel_A for some shapes. kernel_B has worse KV prefetch ordering in our implementation, which can reduce cache locality.
Ada: so the chain is: kernel-affinity tweak -> different kernel chosen for many short requests -> different ordering of KV accesses -> lower hit-rate -> higher batcher wait times -> p95 spike. That tracks.
Devon: ran a bisect across the last 10 commits (range covering PR-9478..PR-9499). `git bisect run ./tools/perf/run_kv_microbench.sh` pointed to commit 8f6d2b6 (PR-9499) as first bad.
Frank: can you paste the offending commit message / diff summary?
Devon: commit 8f6d2b6: "heuristic: prefer affinity_score > 0.7 for kernel_B on short seqs; add tie-break by cost_model_estimate" — small change in kernel selection ordering.
Sasha: repro with a narrow test: forcing kernel_B on short seqs reproduces the hit-rate drop. Forcing kernel_A keeps hit-rate ~82% and p95 ~3.4ms.
Ada: is there a simple mitigation? revert PR-9499 or tweak heuristic to fall back when kv_cache_hit_rate would drop?
Frank: reverting is the fastest to unblock rollout. We should open a hotfix PR that pins kernel selection to the previous behavior and run CI microbenches. I'll prepare revert-9499.
perf-bot: [suggestion] rerun microperf with KV warmup disabled/enabled: `./tools/perf/run_kv_microbench.sh --warmup 5000/20000` to see sensitivity.
Devon: with extended warmup (20k) the hit-rate recovers a bit (-> 70%) but still worse than baseline. So it's not purely cold-start; steady-state is affected.
Sasha: long-term fix: update kernel selector to include a KV-locality score in the affinity calculation. That way cost_model + locality are balanced.
Ada: ok, plan:
- Frank: submit revert PR to restore prior kernel selection ordering (blocking deploy)
- Sasha/Devon: implement locality-aware score and test on dataset + microbenches
- Re-run full CI/perf on revert, confirm p95 back to baseline
Frank: filing revert now: PR-9502 (revert PR-9499). Will add perf benchmark summary in PR description and link ci.perf/9501.
Ada: thx. Once revert PR passes microbench thresholds, we'll un-block the rollout and merge a follow-up with the locality score change behind a flag.
Devon: re-run scheduled: ci.perf/9502 queued. If anyone wants to speed up, I can push a debug build to the internal perf runners.
Frank: pushed revert. CI queued. tagging @Sasha for follow-up patch.
Sasha: got it — I'll start a branch with `affinity += kv_locality_weight * locality_score` and run local microbenches.
Ada: appreciate the quick bisect. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: [ci] PR-9502: build queued
Frank: update: PR-9502 microbench job passed local thresholds on my runner (p95=3.35ms). If CI confirms, we'll merge and roll out.
perf-bot: note: add regression test to microperf that asserts kv_cache_hit_rate >= 75% for kv-batcher workload to catch this class earlier.
Ada: agreed — add that to the microperf golden set. Closing loop when revert merges.
